method: UNSD correspondence table; SKOS whole/narrower distinctions; see DESIGN.md. No applicable standard reference alignment available.

sources.finding: Total consumption is distinct from delivered-to-consumer totals and individual end uses. Historical state groupings and sector changes affect coverage.
Counts of consumers differ from per-consumer averages and sales-only or transportation-only customer groups.
Deliveries for the account of others are transported gas, not total consumption or physical product sales.
Prices have distinct wellhead, citygate, trade and end-user bases. End-user sales prices omit transported-for-others transactions; electric power prices have survey and historical scope limits.

Dry, marketed and gross gas production are whole-gas bases. Well-type withdrawals, removed gases, venting, repressuring and extracted liquids are separate components. State geography changes require history restrictions.
Supplemental supplies include manufactured and biomass gases commingled with natural gas, not total natural-gas production.
Wellhead production value is not consumer expenditure. Reported-volume subsamples differ from total marketed production.
Stock levels differ from injections, withdrawals and net changes. Base and working gas are stock components. US totals exclude Alaska before January 2013.
Total underground storage capacity is distinct from working capacity, facility types and facility counts. US totals exclude Alaska before January 2013.
The subject of exports-by-country is the United States; foreign destinations are partners. LNG and pipeline trade are components.
The subject of imports-by-country is the United States; foreign origins are partners.
Interstate movements and in-transit volumes are not gross international imports/exports. Net flows differ from gross flows.
State tables describe international border-crossing trade, not foreign countries as subjects or state consumption/production.

expectationsBeforeClassifierEdit: Dry, gross and marketed production remain separate labelled whole-gas bases.
Consumer deliveries omit production/transport fuel and cannot replace total consumption.
Named end-use sector totals can fill that sector only. Vehicle fuel alone is not transportation including pipelines.
Customers are counts, not averages, percentages, wells or storage fields. Sales-only/transported-only customers are narrower than sector totals.
Working/base/salt/non-salt stocks and capacity components never replace their total. Storage flows and net changes never become stock levels.
Whole US underground storage and capacity requires periods from 2013; earlier Alaska exclusion remains explicit.
Trade subjects, foreign partners and ports remain distinct. LNG, pipeline, compressed-gas and re-export components do not become total gas trade.
Net imports, interstate flows and in-transit flows do not replace gross international imports or exports.
Wellhead/citygate/import/export prices need separate basis labels. Sector price transactions and survey coverage restrictions remain explicit.
Production value is not consumer expenditure; reported production subsamples are not total production.
Gas plant liquids remain petroleum components even when expressed in gaseous-equivalent units.
Unknown native definitions stay pending; native facet combinations do not prove observations.

historicalScope.reason: Same source gives prior-1997 and through-2000 federal-offshore inclusion statements. Accept neither as whole-state history without reconciliation; post-2000 state scope is separately defined.
Maryland includes DC; Maine includes NH/VT. Source totals are grouped places during these years.
Earlier prices cover regulated electric utilities, not the whole sector; receipt survey population remains restricted afterward.
